title: July 2012 grid collapse
summary: The world's largest blackout: Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern grids failed on consecutive days, cutting supply to over 620 million people across 22 states, with roughly 32 GW of capacity offline. Emblem of the SEB-finances/coal-shortage crisis at baseline.

title: Taper tantrum and rupee crisis
summary: Bernanke's May 2013 taper signal triggered EM capital flight; the rupee fell ~19.4% from 55.4/USD (22 May) to a record 68.85 (28 Aug 2013). Rajan's FCNR(B) swap window from September stabilised it. India branded one of the 'Fragile Five'. CAD compressed from 4.8% (FY13) to 1.7% (FY14) — recovery was underway before the 2014 handover.

sources.name: MoSPI Statistical Year Book, exchange chapter

title: 2010 Kashmir summer unrest
summary: ~112 civilian deaths June-September, triggered by the Machil fake encounter (April) and the killing of Tufail Ahmad Mattoo (11 June). Pellet guns introduced as crowd control in 2010 — a baseline fact for the post-2016 pellet debate.

title: SHRC unmarked graves report
summary: J&K State Human Rights Commission confirmed at least 2,730 unidentified bodies across 38 sites in four north Kashmir districts; 574 later identified as locals, contradicting official claims they were foreign militants. Core human-rights baseline record.

title: Afzal Guru execution and aftermath
summary: Executed at Tihar for the 2001 Parliament attack; Valley-wide curfew and communications blackout followed, at least three protester deaths. Tourism dipped the following seasons. Baseline instance of collective punishment-adjacent curbs predating 2014.

title: Muzaffarnagar riots
summary: Communal violence in western UP killed ~60 and displaced tens of thousands months before the 2014 election. Baseline datum for communal-violence trend analysis, which P-07 complicates.

sources.name: NCRB / MHA data and contemporary reporting

title: National Food Security Act
summary: Statutory entitlement to subsidised foodgrain for ~two-thirds of the population — the capstone of the UPA rights-based welfare architecture (RTI 2005, NREGA 2005, FRA 2006, RTE 2009). The successor government retained and later leaned on it (PMGKAY free-grain top-ups ran on NFSA rails).

title: Devyani Khobragade episode
summary: Arrest and strip-search of India's deputy consul-general in New York over visa-fraud charges triggered retaliatory downgrades of US diplomatic privileges in Delhi — the nadir of a drifting relationship whose 2008 nuclear-deal high was UPA's landmark. Baseline for measuring the post-2014 US arc.

title: Depsang incursion
summary: Three-week platoon-scale PLA presence near Daulat Beg Oldi, resolved 5 May 2013 with mutual withdrawal; Border Defence Cooperation Agreement signed October 2013. Baseline for the post-2014 China arc (Doklam 2017, Galwan 2020) and the border-infrastructure gap.

title: J&K floods and assembly election
summary: September floods killed ~277 and submerged much of Srinagar; the December assembly election recorded 65.91% turnout on the postal-inclusive basis, the highest in ~25 years, producing the PDP-BJP coalition (formed March 2015). The hinge between the baseline and Term 1 Kashmir arcs. Dated to the baseline ledger as state-level events predating the coalition's formation.
caveat: The turnout figure is stated on the postal-inclusive basis and is correct on it. The ECI's own headline for the same election is 65.52%, and both figures are printed in the same ECI statistical report seven pages apart: p.6 HIGHLIGHTS gives 4,794,374 electors who voted AT POLLING STATIONS for 65.52%, and p.13 ELECTORS DATA SUMMARY gives 2,499,904 + 2,294,469 + 1 + 28,402 postal = 4,822,776 for 65.91%. Neither is wrong and neither supersedes the other; a turnout figure for this election is uninterpretable without its basis. The equivalent cannot be computed for the 2024 assembly election, because the ECI has published no statistical report for it or for any of the eight state assemblies polled that year.
